question: Are the displayed scalar x-map polynomials Phi_n and Psi_n^2 already coprime on a locked out-of-sample prime-field panel, with shared-factor and singular-cubic controls?
primary_measurements: numerator and denominator degrees and leading coefficients
monic gcd degree and complete coefficient vector
Euclidean remainder-step and base-field operation counts
primary_acceptance: the numerator and denominator have nominal degrees n^2 and n^2-1
the monic gcd is exactly the constant polynomial one
controls: multiplying both polynomials by X+1 yields monic gcd X+1 in every primary cell
for y^2=x^3 over F_13 and scalar two, the displayed numerator and denominator have a positive-degree monic gcd

implementations.producer: new Rust source using coefficient vectors and Euclidean division
implementations.independent_verifier: separate Rust source with its own polynomial representation, recurrence and gcd

execution.route: isolab EKS Spot after committed source and launch gate

failure_policy: Retain all twelve primary rows and both controls without changing cells, scalars or thresholds after observing affected data.
claim_boundary: Finite exact gcds do not prove generic division-polynomial coprimality or any ECDLP complexity claim.
